A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIPOLE research and contain the main text, eight tables, seven figures, and Appendices A–F. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison, including the content affected by a localized overlap in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original DIPOLE experiments on ExORL, OGBench, and NAVSIM, including benchmark results, ablations, learning curves, and driving cases.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The training losses, linear-guidance sampler, rejection sampling, and DP-VLA/LoRA architecture are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 match; the nonlinear correction added in Appendix B is theoretical, with practical sampling explicitly retaining the existing linear approximation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine ExORL tasks, 30 OGBench single tasks, four OGBench tasks for online fine-tuning, and NAVSIM scenarios with navtrain/navtest rollout variants.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and 7, including CFGRL on ExORL, IDQL on OGBench, and DPPO on NAVSIM. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain the same evaluation metrics, data splits, model configurations, and training budgets, including 1M offline and 1M online RL updates. Experimental settings in Tables 5, 6, and 8 are identical.

E4.justification: The rejection-sampling comparison, Figure 5 hyperparameter analyses, Figure 6 learning curves, and driving cases in Figures 2 and 7 are retained unchanged. The new theoretical discussion introduces no empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both report eight random seeds with means and standard deviations for the principal RL results, and three seeds for Appendix D.4 ablations. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All result tables, plotted results, and qualitative cases match. For example, Table 4 retains PDMS values of 88.3 for DP-VLA, 89.7 for DIPOLE navtrain, and 94.8 for DIPOLE navtest in both versions.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds Eqs. (16)–(19), distinguishing the score identity at t=0 from intermediate scores, presenting an implicit nonlinear correction, and expressing linear guidance as a small-omega approximation. This extends and qualifies the sampling justification; Theorem 1 and its existing proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about stable dichotomous policy learning, controllable greediness through linear score combination, benchmark effectiveness, and scalability to autonomous driving.

C2.justification: V3 newly explains that nonlinear corrected sampling requires expensive neural-network iterations and qualifies direct linear sampling as an approximation when omega is relatively small. V2 lacks this qualification; the empirical interpretations and Appendix F limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and access information are unchanged. The existing project URL moves from the introduction to the abstract without changing its destination or availability claims.

R1.justification: V3 adds Mao et al. (2024), ODICE, in Section 3.1 and Zheng and Lan (2024), Characteristic Guidance, in Appendix B. Other citation changes mainly update publication metadata; the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V3 adds a short Appendix B explanation, relocates the project link, expands funding acknowledgments, and updates bibliography entries. The section organization and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: Local reflow changes spacing and placement around retained material. The learning-curve paragraph moves from page 18 to page 19, where Figure 6 covers several lines in v3. Figures and table structures otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix B now identifies practical sampling as approximate and supplies the nonlinear correction absent from v2, improving theoretical transparency. The gain is limited because the main-text sampling discussion remains unqualified. It outweighs the localized page-19 layout regression, where Figure 6 covers part of its explanatory paragraph while leaving the plots readable.
